stem: What is the primary objective of the Robust principle in the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1?

options.text: To work with current and future browsers and assistive technologies.
options.shortLabel: Compatibility with browsers and assistive tools
options.rationale: Robustness ensures that content uses standard markup so browsers and assistive technologies can interpret it reliably.

options.text: To keep pages loading quickly on slow network connections.
options.rationale: Page load speed is a performance concern, not the WCAG Robust principle.

options.text: To ensure pages link to downloadable accessibility software and browser extensions.
options.rationale: WCAG does not require pages to link to downloadable assistive software.

options.text: To ensure interactive controls show a visible focus indicator.
options.rationale: Visible focus is part of the Operable principle, not Robust.

explanation: The Robust principle mandates that web content must be robust enough to be reliably interpreted by a wide variety of user agents, including current and emerging assistive technologies. This is achieved by using standard markup, complete tags, and accessible name-role-value states.

references.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1: Principle 4 - Robust
